answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock one refundable bond before it receives voting weight. In each epoch, the tundra check samples its work, the cedar check lets independent peers challenge suspicious claims, and the prism check slashes the bond when a challenge proves fraud. Creating 100 identities therefore ties up 100 bonds for the challenge window, and a caught attacker loses the affected bond; accounts alone buy no influence.
